reading.title: The Rise of Mercantilism in Early Modern Europe
reading.passage: Mercantilism, the dominant economic theory from the 16th to 18th centuries, emphasized that national wealth derived from accumulating precious metals and maintaining trade surpluses. European powers competed fiercely to establish colonies and monopolize trade routes, believing that one nation's gain necessarily meant another's loss. This zero-sum economic philosophy drove colonial expansion and shaped international relations for centuries. However, mercantilism eventually declined as economists recognized that mutually beneficial trade could increase wealth for all participants.

writing.prompt: Do you agree or disagree with the following statement? Society should encourage people to reduce their consumption of meat. Use specific reasons and examples to support your answer.
model_sentences: I strongly agree that society should encourage people to reduce their consumption of meat because doing so offers significant environmental and health benefits.
First, reducing meat consumption is crucial for environmental sustainability, as livestock farming generates substantial greenhouse gas emissions and requires vast amounts of water and land.
For example, transitioning to plant-based diets could free up millions of acres of farmland that could be used for carbon-absorbing forests or alternative crops.
Second, consuming less meat directly improves individual health by lowering the risk of heart disease, obesity, and certain cancers that are linked to high meat intake.
Many people who adopt vegetarian or flexitarian diets report experiencing better overall health and increased energy levels within just a few months.
Therefore, encouraging reduced meat consumption through education and policy incentives is a practical step toward building a more sustainable and healthier society for future generations.

speaking.prompt: Some people prefer to spend their money traveling to new places. Others prefer to save their money for the future. Which do you prefer and why? Include specific reasons and details.
model_sentences: I definitely prefer to travel rather than just save money all the time because experiences create lasting memories that savings accounts simply cannot provide.
When you travel, you gain invaluable knowledge about different cultures, meet interesting people, and develop skills that money alone cannot buy, like adaptability and open-mindedness.
For instance, I took a trip to Japan last year, and that experience taught me so much about their culture and changed my perspective on life in ways that really matter.
Of course, saving is important, but I believe the best investment is in enriching your life through meaningful experiences rather than just accumulating money.
So my position is that people should find a balance but prioritize traveling while they're young and healthy, because you can't put a price on those kinds of transformative experiences.

listening.title: History Lecture: The Industrial Revolution
listening.script: Professor: Today, let's discuss the Industrial Revolution, which fundamentally transformed economies and societies between the 1760s and 1840s. The revolution began in Britain and spread throughout Europe and North America. The key innovation was the steam engine, which James Watt improved significantly in 1769. This allowed factories to power machinery at unprecedented scales. Student: Professor, what was the main consequence of this mechanization? Professor: Excellent question. Mechanization shifted production from homes to factories, creating a new industrial working class. Families moved from rural areas to cities seeking factory jobs. This urbanization led to overcrowded cities with poor living conditions. However, it also produced massive increases in productivity and wealth for industrial nations. Student: Did this affect international trade? Professor: Yes, absolutely. Industrialized nations gained competitive advantages, allowing them to dominate global markets and expand their empires. Nations without industrialization fell behind economically and politically. This industrial disparity created the global inequality we still see today.

questions.q: What is the main topic of the lecture?
options: The invention of the steam engine and its creator
The causes and consequences of the Industrial Revolution
The history of urbanization in European cities
The decline of rural economies in the 18th century
questions.explanation: 교수는 산업혁명이 경제와 사회를 어떻게 변화시켰는지에 대해 설명하며, 증기 엔진, 기계화, 도시화, 그리고 국제 무역에 미친 영향을 논의합니다.

questions.q: According to the professor, what was a major consequence of mechanization?
options: Rural farmers became wealthier
Production moved from homes to factories, creating urban working classes
International trade was completely eliminated
European nations stopped competing with each other
questions.explanation: 교수는 기계화가 생산을 가정에서 공장으로 옮겼으며, 이것이 새로운 산업 근로자 계급을 만들었고 도시화를 초래했다고 명확히 설명합니다.

questions.q: Why does the professor mention industrial disparity?
options: To explain why some nations became wealthy while others fell behind
To criticize the British government's policies
To show that all nations industrialized at the same time
To argue that trade was fair and equal
questions.explanation: 교수는 산업화된 국가들이 경쟁 우위를 얻어 세계 시장을 지배할 수 있었던 반면, 산업화되지 않은 국가들은 경제적·정치적으로 낙후되었으며, 이것이 현재의 글로벌 불평등을 초래했다고 설명합니다.
